segments.t: Configure custom AI skills that enhance AI interactions. This tab lets you manage a library of markdown-based skills that are automatically or manually included in AI requests. Open via KTPH001AI → AI Manager → AI SkillsKTPH002; stored in KTPH000.

The skill library used to be a tab in KTPH000Configuration → Global SettingsKTPH001. It now lives in the KTPH002AI ManagerKTPH003, next to profiles, local models and knowledge stores. The stored data and the settings file are unchanged.
korTTY may create skills and save learned rules in them
Local: your own and built-in skills; External: skills imported from the internet
Filters the list by name, description or tags
Opens the usage and size statistics of the skills, see KTPH000Skill statisticsKTPH001
Writes the library to the global settings file

A count line below the list summarizes the whole library — KTPH000TotalKTPH001, KTPH002ActiveKTPH003 (enabled and not hidden), and KTPH004Inactive/hiddenKTPH005 — regardless of the current search or hidden filter.
When you select or create a skill, the right panel shows per-skill fields. Each skill is persisted individually in the skill list.
AI Chat/Functions, AI Agent, Both, Connection

The skill library is stored in KTPH000, which cannot hold certain invisible characters: control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return, U+FFFE, U+FFFF and half of a surrogate pair. Such a character can arrive when you paste into the KTPH002Skill MarkdownKTPH003 editor. A field that contains one shows a message below it that names the character, for example KTPH001, and KTPH004SaveKTPH005 refuses to save the library and selects the skill until you remove the character. When you close the AI Manager with such a skill, korTTY saves your other changes and keeps the last saved version of that skill, or leaves out a skill that was never saved. KTPH006ImportKTPH007 removes such characters from the name, description, tags and Markdown of the imported file.

korTTY ships 39 built-in best-practice skills covering shells (Bash, KornShell, Zsh, Csh, POSIX sh, PowerShell), programming languages (Python, C, C++, Java, C#, JavaScript, Visual Basic, SQL, R, Rust, Go, PHP, Swift, Assembly, Macro Assembler, Ruby, Perl, Lua, Groovy, TypeScript, Kotlin, Dart), markup and data formats (HTML, XML, YAML, JSON) and automation/observability tools (Puppet, Ansible, Azure DevOps Pipelines, Jenkins Declarative and Scripted Pipelines, Filebeat, Logstash). Each skill carries professional guidance on code commenting, robustness, common pitfalls to avoid, and language-specific security practices. They are added to the library on first start and appear with a KTPH000Built-inKTPH001 badge.
Built-in skills behave like your own skills — they can be edited, deactivated and assigned to connections — with these differences:

KTPH000They cannot be deleted, only hidden.KTPH001 KTPH002HideKTPH003 removes a built-in from the list and from all skill pickers, and a hidden built-in is no longer sent with any AI request — even on connections it was previously assigned to. KTPH004Show hidden built-in skillsKTPH005 reveals hidden entries, marked with a KTPH006HiddenKTPH007 badge, so they can be brought back with KTPH008UnhideKTPH009.

KTPH000Unmodified built-ins update automatically.KTPH001 When a new korTTY release ships improved skill content, unchanged built-ins are replaced silently at startup (your Active/hidden choices are kept).

KTPH000Modified built-ins are never touched.KTPH001 Once you edit a built-in it shows a KTPH002Built-in (modified)KTPH003 badge and stops auto-updating. KTPH004Reset to shipped versionKTPH005 discards your changes and restores the delivered version your edits were based on. If a newer delivered version exists, the entry shows 🔄 KTPH006Update availableKTPH007 and KTPH008Update to latest shipped versionKTPH009 adopts it.

KTPH001Your own skills always take precedence.KTPH002 When one of your enabled skills carries a tag matching a built-in's topic (for example a personal skill tagged KTPH000), the built-in is suppressed: it shows KTPH003Overridden by user skillKTPH004, is grayed out, and is no longer sent with any AI request. Deleting or deactivating your skill immediately reactivates the built-in.
Deactivated, hidden and overridden entries are rendered grayed out; this works in every application design theme.

Without auto-detection every enabled skill is sent with every AI request, which would inflate prompts massively with 39 built-in skills. Turning KTPH000Automatically send only matching skillsKTPH001 off therefore asks for confirmation and then deactivates all built-in skills; re-enable the ones you need individually. Built-ins delivered by later releases also arrive deactivated while auto-detection is off.

The KTPH000ExternalKTPH001 view lists skills imported from internet skill directories. External skills live in the same library as your own skills: once you enable one, it is selected and sent exactly like a local skill. The count on each switch button shows how many skills each view holds.
Opens the import dialog: pick a provider, search, preview a SKILL.md and import the selected skills
Asks each external skill's provider for its current version; skills with a newer version show 🔄 KTPH000Update availableKTPH001
Opens the provider table with sign-in details (see below)

korTTY sends a skill's text to the AI model word for word, so a skill from the internet can contain instructions you do not want. Every imported skill therefore arrives KTPH001deactivatedKTPH002, whatever its front matter says. Read it in the editor, then tick KTPH003ActiveKTPH004 and click KTPH005SaveKTPH006. Only the KTPH000 file is imported; scripts, reference files and other files that belong to a skill are never downloaded or run.

When an external skill is selected, the banner above the editor shows its provider, its source and the imported revision. KTPH000Open sourceKTPH001 opens the skill's page in the browser. If you edit the text or the description, the banner and the list mark the skill as KTPH002Changed locallyKTPH003; KTPH004Shorten...KTPH005 never changes the text of an imported skill, only its learned rules. After KTPH006Check for updatesKTPH007 has found a newer version, KTPH008Show update…KTPH009 opens a side-by-side comparison of your version and the provider's version. KTPH010Apply updateKTPH011 replaces the text and description and keeps your name, tags, target, active state and learned rules; a skill imported before descriptions were tracked keeps its description. A skill that is KTPH012Changed locallyKTPH013 is never overwritten, and the dialog says so: it offers KTPH014Import as copyKTPH015, which adds the provider version as a new, deactivated skill named after the revision, and KTPH016Skip this versionKTPH017, which hides that revision while a newer one is still offered. Nothing is updated without a click, and every change takes effect when you click KTPH018SaveKTPH019.

Choose a provider, enter a search and click KTPH001SearchKTPH002. Selecting a result loads its KTPH000 into the preview. The results table shows each skill's name, source, GitHub stars and description; a ✓ before the name marks a skill that is already in the library. Select one or more results and click KTPH003Import selectedKTPH004; results marked ✓ are skipped. What you enter depends on the provider type:

Keywords to search KTPH000 files on GitHub (needs a token), KTPH001 for every skill of a repository, KTPH002 or a GitHub link for one skill; commands copied from agenticskills.io or skills.sh work too
The URL of a KTPH000 file, or a path relative to the provider's base URL

Directories such as agenticskills.io and skills.sh publish their skills as GitHub repositories, so the KTPH003GitHubKTPH004 provider imports from all of them. korTTY reads repositories through the GitHub REST API at KTPH000 (API version 2022-11-28) and remembers the Git revision of each imported KTPH001, so a commit that changes other files of the repository is not reported as an update. Without a token GitHub allows 60 requests an hour; an import takes one or two. GitHub only answers a keyword search with a token: without one, the dialog explains this and offers KTPH005Search SkillsMP insteadKTPH006, which searches the same GitHub skills without signing in. Keywords do not have to match exactly; every word has to appear somewhere in the KTPH002.

The KTPH001SkillsMPKTPH002 provider searches the SkillsMP index through KTPH000. Without an API key SkillsMP allows 50 searches a day, with a key 500. The skills it finds are downloaded from GitHub through the active GitHub provider for github.com, with that provider's token.

KTPH000Providers…KTPH001 opens a table of skill providers that you can extend as you like. korTTY starts with a KTPH002GitHubKTPH003 and a KTPH004SkillsMPKTPH005 provider; add more with KTPH006+ AddKTPH007, for example a GitHub Enterprise server or a team's own server. Deleting a provider keeps the skills imported from it, but they can no longer be checked for updates.
GitHub repository, SkillsMP search, HTTP(S) server
Only active providers appear in the import dialog
Empty uses the type's default (KTPH000, KTPH001); for GitHub Enterprise use KTPH002
None, Token (Bearer), User name and password (HTTP Basic)
Only for User name and password
A GitHub personal access token, a SkillsMP API key or the server password
KTPH000, encrypted with the master password

KTPH000Test connectionKTPH001 checks that the provider answers and accepts the credentials, and shows the remaining request quota where the provider reports one. A token or password is encrypted with the master password when you click KTPH002SaveKTPH003; if the vault is locked, korTTY offers to unlock it. Leave the field empty to keep a stored token, or tick KTPH004Remove stored token/passwordKTPH005 to delete it.

korTTY talks to providers over HTTPS only; plain HTTP is accepted for this computer alone (KTPH000). Redirects are not followed, so a token or password is never sent on to another host, and a KTPH001 larger than 256 KiB is refused.
Skills created by korTTY and learned rulesKTPH000

korTTY can save rules that you confirm into your skills, and it can create a skill for a topic that has none yet. Nothing is saved without your confirmation: the rule card shows the exact text and where it goes, and KTPH000SaveKTPH001 writes it. The switch KTPH002korTTY may create skills and save learned rules in themKTPH003 controls both, and the enterprise policy can lock it.

A rule that names a connection goes into that connection's memory; a rule about a topic that already has a skill, built-in or your own, goes into that skill's learned rules; a rule about a language or tool without a skill creates one; any other rule goes into the global memory. The memory itself is described in KTPH000AI memoryKTPH001.

A skill korTTY created shows the badge KTPH000NEW · created by korTTYKTPH001 until you select it in the list; then it shows KTPH002korTTYKTPH003. The skill the list selects by itself when it opens does not count.
A KTPH000+N rule(s)KTPH001 chip counts the learned rules you have not seen yet; opening the skill marks them as seen and removes the chip.

The editor lists the learned rules of a skill under KTPH000Learned rulesKTPH001, shown only when the skill has any. KTPH002EditKTPH003 changes a rule's text in a dialog, KTPH004DeleteKTPH005 removes it after a confirmation, and both are saved with the skill when you click KTPH006SaveKTPH007.
Learned rules are sent with their skill whenever the skill is selected for a request, as long as the memory is on and the policy allows it.
Rules are proposed from your messages only in the KTPH000Suggest rulesKTPH001 learning mode; KTPH002Remember as rule…KTPH003 saves a rule that you write yourself.

korTTY does not store a possible password, key or token in a skill, a learned rule, the memory or an approved memory file. The check looks for keyword phrases in German and English, KTPH000 assignments (also in KTPH001 files and command-line flags), long random-looking strings, token formats it knows, and values saved in the password vault while the vault is unlocked.

When you change a skill so that it holds a possible secret, KTPH000SaveKTPH001 refuses to save the library and selects that skill. A flagged skill that you do not change does not block KTPH002SaveKTPH003; its badge stays until the secret is removed. The message names the line, the field and the kind of secret, never the value, for example KTPH004Line 4 in the skill text looks like it holds a secret (a password or token assignment). Remove it and try again.KTPH005 A Markdown file or a skill from the internet that holds a finding is refused on import in the same way.

At startup korTTY checks the existing skills and marks one that holds a possible secret with a KTPH000⚠ possible secretKTPH001 badge in the list. It does not change or delete that skill. A flagged skill is still sent with requests until the secret line is removed; only the outbound masking applies.
The check is no guarantee. A password you chose yourself, without a keyword and not saved in the vault, cannot be recognized reliably, so do not write one into a skill.

KTPH001StatisticsKTPH002 in the list's header opens the statistics of your skills: how often each one was sent with a request, how large it is and how that changes. The figures come from the local file KTPH000, see KTPH003Configuration filesKTPH004.
Sets the granularity of the chart and of the size history; the range list follows it
Day: last 30, 90 or 400 days. Month: last 12, 24 or 60 months. Year: all years
Turns recording on or off; while it is off nothing is counted or stored. The enterprise policy can lock it
Also counts the uses of skills that are assigned to a connection or picked explicitly. Off shows automatic uses only
Deletes every recorded use and size history after a confirmation; the skills stay unchanged

The four figures at the top are KTPH000Automatic usesKTPH001, KTPH002Average size of active skillsKTPH003 in tokens, KTPH004Skill tokens sentKTPH005 and KTPH006Growth per monthKTPH007 in tokens per month. The stacked bar chart shows the uses per skill over the range: the eight most used skills and KTPH008OthersKTPH009. The table lists each skill, most used first, with its badge under the name, automatic and pinned uses, average and current size, growth per month and in percent, last use and learned rules. Select a row to see its size history below the table.
KTPH000HintsKTPH001 name the skills to review: one not used for 90 days, one that more than doubled within 30 days, and one above 1,000 tokens. The last two offer KTPH002Shorten...KTPH003.

KTPH000Shorten...KTPH001 asks the default AI profile for a shorter version of the skill and of its learned rules, shows the change as a diff with the token sizes before and after, and saves nothing until you click KTPH002ApplyKTPH003. The text of a skill you wrote yourself can be shortened. For a built-in or an imported skill only its learned rules are shortened, so its text keeps receiving updates. Set a default AI profile first; the dialog says so when none is set.

Daily values are kept for 400 days, monthly values for five years and yearly values without a limit. The enterprise policy key KTPH000 in KTPH001 can switch recording off for everyone; see KTPH002Enterprise policyKTPH003.

When KTPH000Automatically send only matching skillsKTPH001 is enabled, korTTY scores each skill against the current request across four fields — tags, name, description, and the headings in the skill's Markdown — and includes at most the KTPH002twoKTPH003 highest-scoring skills that clear the relevance threshold (ties broken by catalog order). Explicitly pinned and connection-assigned skills are added on top and do not consume that limit. When the local scores are inconclusive (zero or one skill matched, or exactly two matched with nearly equal scores), korTTY additionally asks the model to classify the request and prefers that answer — likewise capped at two skills — falling back to the local result if the call fails. When disabled, all applicable skills are sent without scoring — a skill is still skipped when it is inactive, has empty content, or does not match the current target.
KTPH000AI Chat/FunctionsKTPH001: Skills available in AI Chat and function call contexts
KTPH000AI AgentKTPH001: Skills used by the terminal AI agent
KTPH000BothKTPH001: Available to both AI Chat and AI Agent contexts
KTPH000ConnectionKTPH001: Available to both AI Chat and AI Agent, but only on the connections the skill is assigned to. Such skills are always sent on those connections and bypass auto-detection.

Skills are stored as XML elements within the global settings file. Use KTPH000ImportKTPH001 to load skills from markdown files and KTPH002ExportKTPH003 to save selected skills as markdown files; to import skills from internet directories use the KTPH004ExternalKTPH005 view (see above). KTPH006DeleteKTPH007 applies to your own skills only; built-in skills are hidden instead (see above). Reset, update, hide and unhide are available from the list's context menu and from the banner above the editor when a built-in skill is selected. The skill list can be sorted alphabetically by name or by status (enabled first). KTPH008SaveKTPH009 persists the library immediately and confirms next to the button; pending edits are also written when the AI Manager window is closed. Importing a markdown file always creates an independent user skill — even a file exported from a built-in skill.

This tab manages the global library. Which of these enabled skills apply to a given action is chosen elsewhere: the snippet editor's KTPH000AI skillsKTPH001 picker pins your selection to every snippet AI action, and the KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 window shows the included skills as chips — labelled KTPH004(auto-selected)KTPH005 or KTPH006(manual)KTPH007 — with a searchable picker whose changes take effect on the next re-run. Within snippet AI actions the picker replaces auto-detection: only the ticked skills plus connection-assigned skills are sent, and clearing the picker sends no library skills at all. The snippet KTPH008CorrectKTPH009 and KTPH010TranslateKTPH011 selection actions and the fixed KTPH012DiagramKTPH013 request never include library skills, regardless of target or pinning.
